title: The verifier's ballot admission under definition versions 3 and 4 (ballot version 2): definitions, boards and pinned panels, with the rows 1.3, 2.3, 3.2, 5.1 to 5.5, 5.7 and 6.2 and the report's ballots
generator: packages/crypto/scripts/verifier-ballots-v2-vectors.py, from verifier-ceremony-vectors.py and ballot-v2-vectors.py (independent Python implementations); membership proofs by packages/crypto/scripts/ballot-proofs.mjs, run outside the workspace with Semaphore 4.14.3's depth-32 circuit artifacts and snarkjs 0.7.5, whose groth16.verify gives every pairing verdict on the signals derived here from each record

cases.description: Definition version 3; seat 4 sends nothing, so seats 1 to 3 are registered. The board holds the transcript, an admitted ballot in each cell (both regions of the remainder), a ballot of each admission failure (another election's, cells 3 and 255, a fourth option, a share hash at seat 4, another cell's proof, a proof from a leaf first occurrence zeroed, a changed L1 reference, a vote of 2, an over-vote), two records that don't decode, a re-vote, a byte-identical repeat of the first ballot and the moved member's ballot in its counted cell.
Definition version 3 with only admitted ballots after the transcript: one in each cell and a re-vote. 5.1 to 5.5 and 5.7 pass, and so does 6.2, with no opening on the board.

Copies of the cell 0 ballot: one with the tier 2 ballot's proof (rejected, so it makes no copy a repeat, R4), the original, a copy with its proof negated, the tier 2 ballot, a byte-identical copy and the re-vote (another M). 5.7 rejects the two copies after the original.
The transcript and no ballot: 5.1 to 5.5 and 5.7 pass, with nothing admitted.
Every seat registered: a share hash at seat 4 is admitted.

Definition version 3 pinning spoiled-ballot opening version 1, which can't open version-2 cores: 2.3 fails profile-combination, admission still judges every ballot, and 6.2 is not reached: no opening is judged against an election it can't open the ballots of.
Definition version 4 (receipt keys): ballots are hashed and proved under its version-4 hash, so an admitted version-3 ballot of the same electorate is another election's.
Seats 3 and 4 answer wrongly: no key set is registered, so no ballot or opening is checked.
Ballot version 2's proofs are checked under the same pinned key as version 1's: a definition naming another fails 1.3, and no ballot is checked under it.
The definition gives tier 2's cell a root of 0, which anyone can prove membership of (T-04): no ballot is checked under it.
Definition version 3 pinning ballot version 1, which names a tier, not a cell, beside opening version 1: 2.3 fails profile-combination, and no ballot or opening can be judged against the partition.
Definition version 3 pinning ballot version 5, which a later release may define to name its cell: 2.3, 5.1 to 5.5, 5.7 and 6.2 are unsupported.
